links.reason: 309 and 308 are consecutive lines of one speech; the turn is carried by ஓர் ஊனம் கண்டேன் / ஒட்டினும் ஒட்டேன், but 309 never names whose praise it withholds assent from (யானுங் கண்டேன் அச்சுவ கண்டேன்). 'Qualifies' reads the speaker's own sequence as a limit, and teaches is only a paraphrase of the pair.

2824 describes ascetics who wither the senses (பொறியும் வாட்டி) and guard against lying, killing, theft and lust; it does not say effort is the only road or exclude a god. TM 140 is marked uncertain, and தானே and தன்வசம் can be read two ways, so a clash on who does the work needs generous reading. The 'leaves out a god' and 'school that does not wait for grace' clauses are not in the verses.

1499 உடம்பொழித்தேகுவேனோ means leave the body, i.e. die, in a lover's hyperbole; 1505 ஏகினானே is plain departure by night. The note reads both as 'goes' and sets them as contradictory claims, but neither makes a claim; 1505 simply follows the plot.

The note says in Akananuru 18 the friend's life depends on the heroine's. The Tamil is the friend speaking: ஒருநாள் விழுமம் உறினும் வழிநாள் வாழ்குவள் அல்லள் என் தோழி, meaning the heroine will not live if the hero meets harm. The loyalty runs from the heroine to the lover, so 976's companion does not enact the poem's pledge.

The shared item is a drum proclaiming a wedding (இடிமுரசு அறைந்த / பறையறைந்து). Naladiyar 86 uses it to say a public wedding binds the husband against another's wife, while 1766 summons kings to a choosing; 'guards the bond from later claims' and 'pushes openness' are not in either text.

598 வையம் இன்புறின் மன்னன் இன்புறும் does give the king's side, a fair addition to வானோக்கி வாழும் உலகு / கோல் நோக்கி வாழுங்குடி. But the verse is clipped and its sense flagged uncertain, and its first gains clause (that it lacks the people's dependence) is not what the verse is missing.

1809 recalls a harp-player who won a boon and ruled the northern mountain; 543 has Dharanan come at Nami's song but states no boon, so the 'how the boon was won' step comes from other verses. The line-1 word சயம்பூறான் is unread and the verse is flagged uncertain, so the identification needs reconstruction.

The Tirumanthiram verse says charity removes deep karma and becomes the golden world, so both texts give a better world as fruit; the contrast 'birth vs removal of karma' is overstated. The second gains clause credits TM 1867 with the giver's knowledge of the principles, which is only in 2000 (தத்துவந் தேறி).

The king asking Civakan's clan (குலங்கேட்பான்) and the friends answering is real, but 1856 has Nandattan about to give the lineage (எங்குலம் அடிகள் கேட்க) and the king asks nothing there, so the note's 'king had asked Civakan' and 'he was about to tell' are not what 1856 shows.

63 shows only the queen on the bank and the prince bowing; no slander, procession or giving appears in it, and the accusation is inferred from later verses. Nothing here matches கடுங்குறளை or துளக்கமிலாதவர், so the verse cannot show steadiness under slander.

The patikam's அமிர்து ஈந்த வாறும் is cashed in 947 as பதவமிர்தம் நெஞ்சின் அயின்று, the five-word formula taken to heart, with the dog's body left behind (விட்டு அகன்றது). So the nectar is a teaching, as teaches says.

3107 gives non-injury as protecting others' lives like one's own (தன்னுயிர் ... மன்னுயிர்) with rebirth as reward; 327 says do not kill even at the cost of your own life. The contrast of reward and unconditional rule is real, but 327 does not speak of reward at all and 3107 does not test its rule at the cost of life, so the gains clauses are read in.

149 says one cannot leave the hill-garden without losing life (நீங்க நீங்கும் இன்னுயிர்), an image of its beauty; 201 is the king's own words about leaving Vijayai. Linking the garden's hold to the king handing over rule needs the reader to supply the connection; the Tamil does not.

1296 has the crowd say the king will give the girl to the spear-bearer (நங்கையைக் கொடுக்கும் என்பார்); 1340 has the king decide கொடுப்பது கருமம். The later verse fulfils the earlier prophecy, and the king's own reasoning (ஒப்பினும் உருவினானும்) is added.

17 does show the king's தெளிவின்மை in dharma leading him to take a harmful rite as good, close to கல்லா அரசன் அறம் ஓரான் கொல்லென்பான். But TM 238 is about an unlearned king who says kill, while 17 shows him only setting out; 'led by the people's fear' and 'kills out of duty' are not in 17.

579 is Dharan's maxim that joy comes only after suffering (துன்பமுற்றவர்க்கலால் இன்பமில்லை); Naladiyar 209 is about friends who share joys but not griefs. They share only a friendship theme, and the Naladiyar says nothing of a friend who causes the sorrow, so the 'rule of sharing' limit is read in.

1814 puts a king under a tall umbrella (நெடுங்குடை) as of the moon-line (தண்சுடரோன் வழிமருகன்); the umbrella is not likened to the moon, and the verse does not name the Pandya. Purananuru 3's வெண்குடை உவவுமதி உருவின் is a likeness of the umbrella itself, so the same-image claim and the Pandya identification rest on stretching.

1139 shows a king shattering a diamond pillar; nothing in it is a verdict on anger or on its fruit. Kural 307 says the angry man's ruin is as sure as the hand that strikes the ground, so the note's 'ruin still withheld' is an addition, and the pairing shows only a blow beside a blow.

அணங்கு is truly used of the king to women (157) and of Vijayai to the lotus goddess (162), a real echo. But neither verse says the king is wounded by her, so the second half of teaches goes past the Tamil.

321's line 1 says the killing done once (செய்த ... கொலை) did not end but followed through births; the Kural says killing brings all other deeds. This extends 321 rather than limiting it, and the first gains clause (the verse lacks a general statement) is not shown; line 1 is also flagged hard.

129 says Yugi decides on a trick (விரகினால் பிரித்திடின்); it does not say he judged advising useless, so the contrast with உழையிருந்தான் கூறல் கடன் is supplied. 'Breaks the duty' is the note's judgment, not the verse's.

2822 பிறவற்றின் புண்ணும் ஆந்தி ('eating the wounds of other things') matches the Kural's பிறிதொன்றன் புண்ணது as flesh; the epic adds that such eaters lose விழுப்பயன் and are called வெறுவிலங்கு, which the couplet does not say. The added loss to the eater is a true gain.

2176 does announce the guile of the Videha king (வஞ்சத்தால் சூழ்ந்த வண்ணம்), tied to 2149's கள்ளத்தால் உயிரை உண்ணக் கருதினோம். But teaches leans on verses 2174-2175 that are not in the packet and on the audience/victim contrast, which 2176 does not state.

454 shows women shaping the face's play (முகத்தொழில் வகுத்தார், சிறுநோக்கு), partly matching Siddhar 10's eyes and face shown. But 454 is neutral description and Siddhar 10 does not speak of the epic's skill, so 'what the renunciant fears' and a 'full picture' are read in.

Both poems name Ori (வல்வில் ஓரி in 204's colophon and 209 line 13-14), and Kari's killing him is a stated fact. But this is a shared name, not a shared image, and 209 uses Ori only as a historical reference for Kolli; 'one man's fame as patron and trophy' says little about either poem.

2447 describes the women's longing (கண்விருப்புற்று நோக்கி) and makes no claim; Naladiyar 17 forbids desire. There is no incompatible claim for a tension; the pairing is a theme of desire against old age, and the second gains clause is generic.

393 asks a year without anger (அழற்சி இன்மை) and 407 writes into his mind the policy against enemies; the two are consistent, and the teacher is never called an ascetic. No incompatible claim is made, so 'tension' is not supported; it is a postponement within one plot.

Both verses are about the body at birth, but 2934's அழுதலறி வீழுமே describes helplessness (calling deeds the provision), and does not deny a maker. 'Without a maker' is an argument from silence; TM 451 is also flagged uncertain.

Both have young women weeping over sand figures wrecked by the flood (மணலின் எழுதிய பாவை சிதைத்தது / வண்டல் உய்த்தென அழுது), a real shared image. But 'the akam poet takes a stock festival scene and turns it' asserts a derivation neither text shows.

The lamp-and-smoke apology (புகை ... விளக்கை இகழ்வார் இல்லை) is nearly identical in both. But the 'different request' of each poet is not shown: both ask hearers who grasp the meaning to accept the work, so teaches is an overstatement.

690 sends the envoys back defiantly; 1210 says by custom envoys are not harmed (தூதுவர் முறைப்படும்), so a fault is borne. The link is real but the speaker of 1210 is uncertain and may not be the hero, so 'the hero shown lawful' is conjecture.
1782 has the hall finished and 1783 the hour and the kings' entry; this is story order only and nothing in 1783 answers or fulfils 1782. 'Develops' dresses sequence as a link.

724 has the gods marvel that a lion able to kill a thousand was overcome; Naladiyar 198 holds the lion's strength as the measure of a man who would die poor before shame. They share a lion, not a claim, and 'strength is not a single measure' is a theme.

1844 and 1851 are neighbouring verses of one speech by Payapati, both using the root of good deeds (நல்வினை முதல்). Repeated in one passage, this shows emphasis, not a link, and 'the king returning to the same fear' is the note's reading.

1546 gives gladly giving to ascetics as dana and abstaining from honey, toddy and meat as sila; it says nothing of the giver's own fasts or of 'four equal duties'. Kural 263's chiding question is about those who forgo tapas for providing, so the epic does not answer it.

2022 has Suramanjari scoff that a dead tree revives by rain; Naladiyar 11 says grey hair will come, the wise renounce young. These do not clash: youth passing and not returning agree, and the disguise story is not in the verse, so teaches relies on plot outside it.

97 shows the queen's thought of the singer (நெஞ்சத்து இருத்தினள்); 117 she leaves while the king lies still (உறங்குதல் புரிந்த போழ்தின் ... பெயர்ந்து). The desire-to-deed step is real, but it is the plot's order and the keeper is not named in 117.

785 has the companions born the very day Civakan was (ஒருங்கவன் பிறந்த ஞான்றே); 1793 recasts that day as the king's death (இறைவன் வீடிய அஞ்ஞான்றே) and takes the guilt (எங்கள்வினையால்). The reframing is stated in the Tamil, so the later verse develops the earlier.

213 holds pleasures and life-days measured by past penance (அளந்தன போகம்); Kural 377 has வகுத்தான் apportion, an agent not named in 213, so the two doctrines differ. The first gains clause is generic, and 'couplet open to misuse' is the note's gloss, not shown by the epic.

The two lists overlap only in the destitute, the young and perhaps the bereaved; Acharakkovai also frees the stranger, the one who has eaten, the king's worker and the bridegroom, who are not weak, and Elathi names the unseen and the excellent. 'Nearly the same weak persons' is false, and the two books make different claims.

Kural 375's ஆக்கம் is about wealth-making, where good means turn bad, not about merit and reward. 169 asks to ponder the envious man's gain and the good man's loss. 'Agree' on outcomes not tracking merit is overstated, and the note relies on a commentator.

129 and 282 both close the description of a wishing-tree place with a rhetorical question, pattern X ஆவன Y. The two verses are not shown to describe the same ridge, so 'the ridge's beauty used to move a decision' is read in.

1948 மின்னி னீள்கடம்பின்னெடு வேள்கொலோ / மைந்தனோ is the same first-sight 'is he this or that' perplexity as 1081 அணங்குகொல் ஆய்மயில் கொல்லோ. Their form agrees but 'qualifies' does not fit, and the gains clauses about a convention and a plural speaker are generic.
